spans.text: Aspects of gods come in many forms (described in Lyre’s Guide to Retia’s Divinity chapter), but the simplest understanding of them is that an aspect is an incomplete incarnation of a deity, which may appear in a realm outside their own. Some gods are only as powerful as their aspects, but many (such as the Eidolons) have such incomprehensible power that any version of them appearing outside their own divine realm is likely to be lacking the power of the full god - an honor reserved for when they appear in the flesh, or exist within their own divine realm.

A god may wish to incarnate as an aspect for one of many reasons - they might not wish to risk their own physical form for example, since the loss of an aspect is only a hindrance and not a true casualty. They may also only be able to manage to project an aspect of themselves because their full might cannot appear beyond the Divine Curtain. This is true of all of the Eidolons, who cannot pass through without the Curtain being parted for them. They may also choose to appear as an aspect because it embodies a unique facet of them, such as representing their role as a god of honor, necromancy, etc. These aspects might carry themselves differently than the god as a whole, and sometimes may have entirely different personalities. Finally, an aspect may physically be assigned to a task as an autonomous extension of a god, and it must carry out its duties so that the god as a whole need not pay direct attention.
